title: Guide Garden — Quick Jotter for Docs & SDK Fixes
body:
Context:
This is my messy scratchpad for the next docs sprint — focused on small, high-impact fixes in SDK tutorials and sample apps. Keep everything loose here: repro notes, tiny patches, and what to prioritize for the upcoming docs pairing session.

Goals (short):
- Ship fixes that unblock first-time users in tutorial flow (install -> run sample -> streaming chat).
- Reduce triage time for streaming-related issues by adding a short troubleshooting section.
- Add 2 minimal sample apps: (1) streaming chat w/ fallback and (2) embeddings cache example.

High-level priorities (this week):
1) Streaming tutorial: clearly document env vars + common firewall/timeouts (P0)
2) Sample app: streaming fallback (P1)
3) Quick embedding cache example + config snippet (P1)
4) Small copy fixes across README examples (P2)

Immediate TODOs / notes to self:
- Reproduce DEVX-428 (Streaming stops mid-response): steps below. (assigned: me)
- Add small troubleshooting block: "Common causes of truncated streams" in tutorial page. (Sofia to review)
- Write tiny sample: embeddings-cache.js (Node) — show TTL=60s, LRU with max 500 items. (Eve to prototype)
- Update SDK quickstart: include curl + Python snippet for streaming and non-streaming side-by-side.
- Add one-line note about API surface parity between hosted and dedicated in the tutorial (callout).

Repro steps for streaming-truncation (DEVX-428):
1) Start local sample server (node sample/streaming-chat) with REDWOOD_API_KEY set to test key.
2) Use client-side code (Node stream mode):
   const resp = client.chat.stream({ messages });
   resp.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk));
3) Send a long prompt (>= 800 tokens) with forced backoff (client simulated latency).
4) Observe: stream ends with "[EOF]" then client emits 'close' but the final tokens are missing.
5) Server logs show a truncated write to socket at approx 3.8s.

Hypothesis & quick checks:
- Hypothesis A: server-side batching heuristics escalate to a non-streaming path when latency spikes -> missing final chunk.
  Quick check: toggle BATCHER_STRICT=false locally -> see if behavior changes.
- Hypothesis B: client abort on idle timeout (default 5s) -> adjust CLIENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT=12s.
  Quick check: increase timeout and repro.
- Hypothesis C: proxy (corp gateway) killing long-lived chunked responses -> ask SRE to check ingress logs for 502/timeout.

Quick notes for the doc text (phrasing ideas):
- "If your stream cuts out early: try increasing CLIENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT, and verify your gateway allows chunked transfer for >15s windows."
- Add a diagnostic command: curl --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -d '{"messages":[...]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream | sed -u 's/\r//' | tail -n 20

Small sample app plan (streaming fallback):
- Flow: attempt streaming call -> on stream error or EOF without finalizer, call non-streaming /chat/generate with same prompt, merge outputs.
- Files to add: sample/stream-fallback/app.js, README.md (2 small commands to run)
- Edge cases: double-billing risk (user might be charged twice). Add note: "use short max_tokens in fallback or server-side idempotency token."

Embeddings cache example (Node) minimal code idea:
- Use a tiny LRU cache wrapper around client.embeddings.generate():
  - show TTL config and comment about storage backends (redis vs in-memory)
- Example snippet to include in docs.

Copy nits I keep encountering (quick fixes list):
- Quickstart page: command uses old env var REDWOOD_KEY -> update to REDWOOD_API_KEY.
- SDK example: uses client.generate() in some places, client.chat.create() in others -> standardize to client.chat.create for chat flows.
- Typos: "paramater" -> parameter (three pages).

Open questions / blockers:
- Do we want to surface the Dedicated vs Hosted differences more prominently in the quickstart? (Product input needed)
- Billing/duplicate-call note for streaming fallback: should legal sign-off be required? (ask Kate in PM sync)
- SRE help required to rule out network proxy as cause of truncation.

Meeting prep for Wed pairing (30 min):
- Agenda: 1) reproduce streaming truncation (live) 2) pair on fallback sample 3) align copy for quickstart.
- Bring: local machine with node 18, test key, and a terminal.

One-off scribbles / things to remember:
- Consider adding a "when to use streaming" callout with measured latency examples (p95 tokens/sec) vs non-streaming.
- Add a simple diagram: client -> router -> model pool -> fallback router. Keep it 1 image, 3 boxes.
- Add a note to Console team: can we expose per-request "stream health" metric? (ask via slack #observability)

Patch checklist before PR: (short)
- [ ] small unit test for fallback behavior (simulate stream error)
- [ ] README step-by-step verified on mac + linux
- [ ] minimal CHANGELOG entry: "docs: streaming tutorial fixes"

If stuck: revert to micro-PRs. One tiny change per PR (env var, copy, sample file). Faster reviews.

-- end of page --
